rights_basis: Statements quote the 16th-century Nahuatl and Spanish transcription columns (public domain) from hash-pinned witnesses, with an independent English rendering. The modern Anderson & Dibble and Garcia Garagarza translations were consulted for verification only and are not reproduced beyond bracketed-emendation facts.
scope_note: Chapters 1-38 of Florentine Codex Book 4, covering all twenty trecenas (One Cipactli through One Rabbit), from hash-pinned folios 1r-71r. Each statement quotes one witness record and is rendered independently into English. Trecena membership lists are cross-checked against the validated tonalpohualli kernel, and disagreements are recorded as witness variants rather than corrected. The pack quotes the corpus; it never assigns a day sign to a birth, because no civil-date correlation is approved - and, as folios 21r, 35v, 52v and 55v show, the tradition itself assigned the operative sign by ritual choice and household means rather than by date of birth.

statements.nahuatl: Injc ce capitulo, itechpa tlatoa, injc centetl machiotl: in jtoca ce cipactli, ioan in qualli tonalli in qujmaceoaia, in vncan tlacatia, in toqujchti, in cioa: can iehoantin qujpoloaia, qujmotlacalhujaia, yn jpampa in jntlatziviliz.

spanish_parallel.excerpt: Capitulo I del primero signo, llamado Ce Cipactli, y de la buena fortuna que tenian los que en el nacian, ansi hombres como mujeres, si no la perdian por su negligencia o floxura

statements.engine_rendering: First chapter, which tells of the first sign, named One Cipactli, and of the good day-fortune that those born then merited, men and women alike: yet these same people could destroy it, could forfeit it by their own act, because of their laziness.
statements.doctrinal_note: The conditionality is in the chapter heading itself, in both languages: the fortune is merited (qujmaceoaia) and can be lost through one's own negligence (tlatziviliz / floxura). Any rendering of this corpus as an unconditional trait table misstates the source from its first sentence.

statements.nahuatl: Injn matlactetl vmei in tonalli, in iuhquj itlavilanoan muchioa, yn jtech povi: iehoatl in vme acatl, ey calli, navi cuetzpali, macujlli coatl, chiquacen mjqujztli, chicome macatl, chicuei tochtli, chicunavi atl, matlactli itzcujntli, matlactli oce ocomatli, matlactli vmome malinalli, matlactli omej acatl.
statements.engine_rendering: These thirteen days become as its dependents, belonging to it: Two [Wind], Three House, Four Lizard, Five Serpent, Six Death, Seven Deer, Eight Rabbit, Nine Water, Ten Dog, Eleven Monkey, Twelve Grass, Thirteen Reed.

witness_variant.reading: The witness writes 'vme acatl' (Two Reed) as the second member, where the cycle requires Two Wind (ecatl); the list closes correctly with 'matlactli omej acatl' (Thirteen Reed).
witness_variant.assessment: Near-certain scribal variant for 'vme ecatl'. The standard scholarly translation emends to 'Two [Wind]' in brackets with a note, which independently confirms this reading. Preserved here rather than silently corrected.
witness_variant.kernel_crosscheck: The validated tonalpohualli kernel gives trecena 1 as coefficients 1-13 over signs cipactli, ehecatl, calli, cuetzpalin, coatl, miquiztli, mazatl, tochtli, atl, itzcuintli, ozomatli, malinalli, acatl - agreeing with the witness list at every position except the attested variant.

statements.nahuatl: In jzqujtetl in tonalli: iuh mjtoaia, muchi qualli: in aqujn ipan tlacatia pilli; mjtoaia tecutiz, tlatocatiz, motlacamatiz, mocujltonoz, motlamachtiz: Auh intla maceoalli ipan tlacatia, oqujchtiz, tiacauhtiz, maviztiz, panvetziz, motleiotiz, onca qujquanj iez: auh intla cioatl ipan tlacati, no motlacamatiz,
statements.engine_rendering: All of these days, it was said, were entirely good. He who was born then a noble, it was said, would become a lord, would rule, would be obeyed, would be rich, would prosper. And if a commoner were born then, he would become a man, a brave warrior, honored, risen high, renowned; he would have food to eat. And if a woman were born then, she too would be obeyed,
statements.doctrinal_note: The augury is stratified by social station and sex - noble, commoner, woman each receive a distinct formulation of the good fortune. Flattening these into one trait erases the source's own structure. The woman's augury continues onto folio 2r: she prospers, feeds people, hosts, is obeyed; through her the suffering are refreshed; her marketplace dealings succeed.

statements.nahuatl: Auh no yoa quitoaia: ma nel ivi in qualli itonal ipan otlacat, intlacamo vellamaceoa, intlacamo vel monotza, intlacamo qujcuj, intlacamo itech qujpachoa, in atl cecec, in tzitzicaztli, yn inonotzaloca, in izcaliloca, in veuetlatolli, yn jlamatlatolli, in can tlaueliloti, tlavelilocati, in can aie vtli qujtoca, atle onqujca, can ynevian mopopoloa,
statements.engine_rendering: And they also said: even though he was born on a good day sign, if he does not do penance well, if he does not take counsel with himself, if he does not accept and apply to himself the cold water and the nettle - the admonitions, the instruction, the words of the old men and the old women - if he merely turns corrupt, becomes wicked, follows no road at all: nothing comes of it; he destroys it entirely by his own doing.
statements.doctrinal_note: The forfeiture clause. 'The cold water, the nettle' (in atl cecec, in tzitzicaztli) is the standard Nahuatl difrasismo for corrective discipline. This paragraph is the doctrine the defensibility spec ordered preserved: the day sign grants a potential that conduct completes or destroys. It is the structural opposite of a personality trait.

statements.nahuatl: in jtoca ce ocelutl: ioan in amo qualli tonalli, in qujmomaceviaia in aqujque ipan tlacatia, in toqujchti, in cioa: auh tel in jca innezcaliliz, in vel nenotzalizpatia: auh in aqujque in jpan tlacatia, y, achi muchintin tlatlacoti muchioaia.

spanish_parallel.excerpt: Ocelutl, y de la mala fortuna que tenian los que en el nacian, ansi hombres como mujeres, si con su buena diligencia no se remediaban. Los que en este signo nacian por la mayor parte eran esclavos

statements.engine_rendering: ...the sign named One Ocelot: and of the bad day-fortune that those born on it merited, men and women alike - and yet it was healed by their rearing, by taking counsel with themselves well; and of those born on it, very nearly all became slaves.
statements.doctrinal_note: The second chapter is the mirror image of the first: a bad sign whose heading carries its own remedy clause. 'auh tel in jca innezcaliliz, in vel nenotzalizpatia' - 'and yet, by their upbringing, it was cured by taking good counsel with oneself' - is a conditional, and the Spanish column renders the same clause as 'si con su buena diligencia no se remediaban'. A bad sign is a liability to be worked against, not a verdict. The heading begins on folio 3v ('Injc vme capitulo... injc vntetl ma[chivtl]') and is completed here; the bracketed syllable is the Getty edition's reconstruction of the word broken across the folio turn.

statements.nahuatl: qujcenvica, qujcentlaca, yn itlavilan matlactli vmei, in jtech povi, iehoantin, y, vme quauhtli, ei cozcaquauhtli, navi olin, macujlli tecpatl, chiquacen qujavitl, chicome xochitl, chicuey cipactli, chicunavi hecatl, matlactli calli, matlactli oce, cuetzpali, matlactli vmome coatl, matlactli vmei mjqujztli:
statements.engine_rendering: It carries them all with it, it casts them all together, its thirteen dependents that belong to it, these: Two Eagle, Three Vulture, Four Movement, Five Flint, Six Rain, Seven Flower, Eight Cipactli, Nine Wind, Ten House, Eleven Lizard, Twelve Serpent, Thirteen Death.
statements.doctrinal_note: Kernel cross-check: the validated tonalpohualli kernel gives trecena 2 as coefficients 1-13 over ocelotl, cuauhtli, cozcacuauhtli, ollin, tecpatl, quiahuitl, xochitl, cipactli, ehecatl, calli, cuetzpalin, coatl, miquiztli. The witness agrees at every one of the twelve listed positions. Note that this list spells the wind sign 'hecatl' (chicunavi hecatl), which is independent support for reading the folio 1v 'vme acatl' as a slip for 'vme ecatl'.

statements.nahuatl: Auh intlanel aca tiacauh, oquichtli, tlamanj muchioaia, vel monamacaia, motlacocaoaia, tevic, temecapal muchioaia, victli, mecapalli qujmottitiaia, iuh mjtoaia: ca iuhquj itonal, iuhquj iol, iuhquj ipan tlacat, iuhquj itlacatiliz:
statements.engine_rendering: And even though someone became a brave warrior, a man, a taker of captives, he would sell himself, would sell himself cheap; he became another's digging stick, another's tumpline; the digging stick and the tumpline showed themselves to him. Thus it was said: such was his day sign, such his life, such the day he was born on, such his birth.
statements.doctrinal_note: This is the corpus at its most fatalistic, and it must be quoted rather than softened: the fourfold 'iuhquj' formula asserts that the outcome simply is the day sign. The very next paragraph on the same folio reverses it for the diligent man, and the two stand together in the source. Presenting either one alone misrepresents the chapter.

statements.nahuatl: auh ca vei qujcaia in aca tiacauh, amo monamacaia, in jvian oalnemja tlalticpac: iehoatl in amo tlatziuhquj, in jeel, in tlamocujtlavianj, in cochicanj, in tlacelianj, in tlamaceoanj, in mocaoanj, in mjconj, in tlachpananj, in tlatzetzeloanj, in tlacujcujnj, in tletlalianj, in ioalli qujtztoc, in popoxiuhteoa, in mocujtivetzi, in amo moteteca, in amo moxiccaoa,
statements.engine_rendering: But a brave man could come out well indeed; he did not sell himself, he went on living at his ease upon the earth - that is, the one who was not lazy: the diligent one, the careful one, who woke early, who received instruction, who did penance, who fasted, who drew his own blood, who swept, who shook out the dust, who scoured, who laid the fire, who watched through the night, who rose stirring the embers, who seized his work at once, who did not sprawl idle, who did not neglect himself...
statements.doctrinal_note: The escape clause of the worst trecena in the book, and it is not framed as luck: it is a list of practices - rising early, sweeping, fasting, autosacrifice, night vigil, accepting instruction. Book 4 locates the difference between two people born on the same day in what they did, not in what they were.

statements.nahuatl: Ioan iehoatl qujcaia, panvetzia, in vel monotza, in tlacacquj, in amo qujquammati, qujtemati in onotzaloca, izcaliloca, ican itech qujpachoa, ican qujmacuj, qujmapiquj: auh intla ica necacaiaoalo, amo qujtecuepiliaia, amo qujcuepcaiotia, atle ic qujlochtia.
statements.engine_rendering: And this one came out well, rose high: the one who took counsel with himself, who listened, who did not take it as wood, who valued being admonished and instructed, who pressed it to himself, who took it in his hand, who held it closed in his fist. And if he was mocked, he did not turn it back on them, did not repay it, did not retaliate at all.
statements.doctrinal_note: 'qujquammati' - literally 'takes it as wood', i.e. hears correction as an insult - is the vice named here; its opposite, 'qujmapiquj' (he closes his hand upon it), is the virtue. The augury is therefore about the reception of counsel, which no birth-date lookup can supply.

statements.nahuatl: no iuhquj ipan mitoaia in aqujn ipan tlacati, ca moch vel qujchioaz in toltecaiotl, vel totoltecatiz, tlatlanemjliz, ioiolizmatquj iez, intla uel monotzaz: auh intlacamo vel monotza, atle onqujcaia, atle icnopil, can iaujlqujzca, iquequeloloca in qujmomaceviaia.
statements.engine_rendering: The same was said of whoever was born on it: that he would do all the craft-work well, would be a true master craftsman, would be inventive, would be quick-witted - if he took counsel with himself well. And if he did not take counsel with himself well, nothing came of it, there was no deserving; what he merited was only his own dishonour, his own derision.
statements.doctrinal_note: A day-level (house-level) augury inside a trecena, showing that the conditional structure is not confined to chapter headings. Seven Flower is the embroiderers' and craftworkers' day; folio 6r sets out the fasts they kept for it and states that a craftswoman who spoiled her fast earned 'avilquizcaiotl' - dissoluteness - on the very same day. Same day, opposite outcomes, decided by observance.

statements.nahuatl: Injc ei capitulo, itechpa tlatoa: injc etetl machiotl, in jtoca ce macatl: yoan in qualli tonalli, in qujmomaceviaia yn ipan tlacatia, in toqujchti, in cioa: auh intlacamo inpan neltiaia, can iehoantin in tlatziviliztica qujpoloaia.

spanish_parallel.excerpt: Capitulo III del tercero signo, llamado Ce Mazatl, y de la buena fortuna que tenian los que en el nacian, ansi hombres como mujeres, si por su negligencia no la perdian

statements.engine_rendering: Third chapter, which tells of the third sign, named One Deer, and of the good day-fortune that those born on it merited, men and women alike; and if it was not fulfilled in them, it was they themselves who destroyed it, by laziness.
statements.doctrinal_note: The same conditional shape as chapter 1, in almost the same words: 'intlacamo inpan neltiaia' - if it was not made true in them. The fortune is a claim on conduct, and the Spanish column agrees ('si por su negligencia no la perdian').

statements.nahuatl: qujvica, iehoatl in vme tochtli, ey atl, navi itzcujntli, macujlli ocomatli, chiquacen malinalli, chicome acatl, chicuei ocelotl, chicunavi quauhtli, matlactli cozcaquauhtli, matlactli oce olin, matlactlomome tecpatl, matlactlomei qujavitl.

statements.doctrinal_note: Kernel cross-check: trecena 3 runs mazatl, tochtli, atl, itzcuintli, ozomatli, malinalli, acatl, ocelotl, cuauhtli, cozcacuauhtli, ollin, tecpatl, quiahuitl. The witness agrees at all twelve listed positions.

statements.nahuatl: In jzqujtetl in tonalli, mjtoaia: qualli, ieccan: auh tel cequj iitla actiuh, itzalan actiuh, injc itlacauhtiuh, in iuh moteneoaz: vncan mjtoa inneneixcaujltoca, injc tecpantivi:
statements.engine_rendering: All of these days were said to be good, a favourable place; and yet some go with something inside them, something lodged among them, so that they go spoiled, as will be told: there the particular names of each are given, in the order they are set out.
statements.doctrinal_note: The corpus explicitly refuses to treat a 'good' trecena as uniformly good: 'auh tel cequj iitla actiuh, itzalan actiuh, injc itlacauhtiuh'. A rendering that reports a trecena as simply fortunate contradicts the source's own qualification.

statements.nahuatl: in aqujn ipan tlacati pilli, in tetzon, in teizti, in tetzicueuhca, in tetzicueoallo, in tetlapanca, in tetechpa qujz, iol, in teujtztzo, in teaoaio, in tetentzon, in teixquamol, in teezco, in tetlapallo, tlatocaiotia, oalmoteniotiaia, ipal atlioaia, ipallaqualoia, tetlauhtiaia, qujtemacaia, tetech qujtlaliaia in tilmatli, in maxtlatl, in tlalpilonj, in tecacatl, in nacochtli:
statements.engine_rendering: He who was born on it a noble - hair of someone, fingernail of someone, chip and splinter and fragment of someone, sprung and born from someone, thorn of someone, spine of someone, beard of someone, eyebrow of someone, blood and colour of someone - was made a ruler, gained a name, by him men drank and ate; he made gifts, he gave things away, he placed upon people the cape, the loincloth, the head-band, the lip-plug, the ear-plug.
statements.doctrinal_note: The heaped metaphors for descent (hair, nail, splinter, thorn, blood of someone) are the standard Nahuatl idiom for legitimate lineage. The augury is addressed to a social station first and a person second: the following paragraphs give separate formulations for the commoner and for the woman.

statements.nahuatl: Auh no ioan mjtoa: in aqujn ipan tlacati ce macatl: qujlmach cēca momauhtiaia, can jmaviz in qujmattinenca, can imauhcac in nemja, can mamauhcanenca, vel iolmjquja, in jquac qujcaquja
statements.engine_rendering: And it is also said: whoever was born on One Deer, it is told, was greatly afraid; he went about knowing only dread, he lived only in his fear, he went about only frightened, he quite fainted with terror when he heard...
statements.doctrinal_note: An honest counterweight: not every Book 4 augury is conditional. Here the sign's animal supplies a disposition directly, by likeness ('es su natural del ciervo ser temeroso' in the Spanish column), and the chapter goes on to say the parents took no trouble over such a child. Encoding only the conditional passages would flatter the corpus; both patterns are present and both are quoted.

statements.nahuatl: Inic chicome capitulo, itechpa tlatoa: injc nauhtetl machiotl, yn jtoca ce xuchitl: auh in toqujchti ipan tlacatia, qujtoaia: qujlmach papaqujnj iez, vel mozcalianj: ioan vel qujmocujtlavia in cujcatl, ioan in paqujliztli, ioan cacamanaltinj, cacamanale: auh qujl in cioa, vevey tlamachiuhque: qujlmach can tlanepantla ca injn machiotl, qujtoznequj achi tetolinj, ioan achi qualli.

spanish_parallel.excerpt: Capitulo VII del cuarto signo, llamado ce xuchitl. Los hombres que nacian en el decian que eran alegres, inginiosos y inclinados a la musica y a placeres, decidores, y las mujeres grandes labranderas, y liberales de su cuerpo si se descuidaban. Decian este signo ser indiferente a bien y a mal

statements.engine_rendering: Seventh chapter, which tells of the fourth sign, named One Flower. And of the men born on it they said: it is told he would be joyful, quick-witted, and would take good care of song and of gladness, and would be a joker, a teller of tales; and it is told the women were great embroiderers. It is told this sign stands in the middle, which is to say somewhat afflicting and somewhat good.
statements.doctrinal_note: 'can tlanepantla ca' - it stands right in the middle. Book 4 has a three-valued vocabulary for signs (qualli / amo qualli / tlanepantla), and this chapter names the middle term explicitly. Any two-valued good/bad presentation loses a category the source itself uses.

statements.nahuatl: Moquetza ce suchitl, ioan yn jzquitetl ytlavilanoan: injc matlactetl omei tonalli muchiuhtica in yehoatl contoqujlia vme cipactli, yoan ey acatl, navi calli, macujlli cuetzpali, chiquacen coatl, chicome mjqujztli, chicuei macatl, chicunavi tochtli, matlactli atl, matlactli oce ytzcujntli, matlactlomome ocomatli, matlactlomey malinalli:
statements.engine_rendering: One Flower rises up, and all its dependents: it is made up of thirteen days, that which follows it being Two Cipactli, and Three [Wind], Four House, Five Lizard, Six Serpent, Seven Death, Eight Deer, Nine Rabbit, Ten Water, Eleven Dog, Twelve Monkey, Thirteen Grass.
statements.doctrinal_note: Two independent occurrences of acatl written for ehecatl (folios 1v and 16v) suggest a habit of this Nahuatl scribe rather than a single slip; in both cases the correct sign is recoverable from the cycle and, here, from the facing Spanish column.

witness_variant.reading: The Nahuatl column writes 'ey acatl' (Three Reed) at the third position, where the cycle requires Three Wind (ehecatl); Reed cannot fall in this trecena at all.
witness_variant.assessment: This is the same substitution the pilot found on folio 1v ('vme acatl' for 'vme ecatl'), recurring here in a different chapter. Decisively, the Spanish column of the same folio gives the correct reading - 'la tercera, yei ecatl' - so the two columns of the same page disagree, and the error is confined to the Nahuatl scribe. Preserved rather than silently corrected.
witness_variant.kernel_crosscheck: The validated kernel gives trecena 4 as xochitl, cipactli, ehecatl, calli, cuetzpalin, coatl, miquiztli, mazatl, tochtli, atl, itzcuintli, ozomatli, malinalli. The witness agrees at every position except the attested acatl/ehecatl variant.

statements.nahuatl: auh qujttaia, qujmaceoaia in jneiollaliliz, in jnetlamachtil, pactinenca, vellamatia: in jquac ipan mjmatia ytonal, qujtoznequj: in jquac vel monotzaia, in vel ontlamaceoa.
statements.engine_rendering: And he saw and merited his consolation, his prosperity; he lived contented, he was well pleased - when he was careful of his day sign, which is to say: when he took counsel with himself well, when he did penance well.
statements.doctrinal_note: The source glosses its own term. 'ipan mjmatia ytonal' (he was prudent regarding his day sign) is defined on the spot as taking counsel with oneself and doing penance. Devotion to the sign is thus described as conduct, not as belief or luck.

statements.nahuatl: Auh in aqujn amo ipan mjmatia, in atle ipan qujttaia: can qujtlavelia yn jtonal: ca iuh mjtoa: in jquac aqujn cujcanj, anoco aca toltecatl, tlachichiuhquj: intla ie vnca qujquanj, ye vnca ynecujltonol: auh ie conpopoa, ijxco, ijcpac, ie qujmana, contepopoaltia, yz ic moquetza, iz ic moqujxtia, ic teijxco, teicpac nemj, ic atlamattinemj, ic cuecuenoti,
statements.engine_rendering: But as for the one who was not careful of it, who regarded it as nothing: he merely turns his day sign hostile. For thus it is said: when a singer or some craftsman, some maker, already has food to eat, already has his wealth - and then he counts it his own, he sets it before his face and above his head, he makes people count it, and by it he stands up and sets himself apart, and so goes about in people's faces and over their heads, goes about presuming, becomes arrogant...
statements.doctrinal_note: 'can qujtlavelia yn jtonal' - he simply makes his own day sign hostile. Book 4's failure mode is not that a bad sign strikes; it is that a person spoils a good one. The chapter then follows the arrogant craftsman all the way to disease, abandonment and a pauper's death on folio 17v, and the Spanish column states plainly that this happened to him 'por haber perdido la ventura de su signo'.

statements.nahuatl: Injc chicuei capitulo: itechpa tlatoa, injc macujltetl machiotl, in jtoca ce acatl: auh amo qualli tonalli in jtech ca, qujlmach in aqujque vncan tlacatia, intla vncan tlacatia, injc chicunauhtetl calli, in jtoca chicunavi cipactli: qujtoaia qujlmach cenca techicoitoanj, ioan teteixpanvianj: auh qujlmach injn machiotl, iehoatl itonal in quetzalcoatl: ipampa in tlatoque, in pipilti, vncan muxtlaoaia ioan tlamanaia.

spanish_parallel.excerpt: Capitulo VIII del quinto signo, llamado ce acatl, mal afortunado. Decian que los que nacian en el, especial si nacian en la nona casa, que llaman chicunahui cipactli, eran grandes murmuradores, noveleros, malsines, testimuneros

statements.engine_rendering: Eighth chapter, which tells of the fifth sign, named One Reed: and the day-fortune upon it was not good. It is told that those who were born then - if they were born in the ninth house, named Nine Cipactli - they said, it is told, that they were great slanderers and great accusers. And it is told that this sign was the day sign of Quetzalcoatl; for that reason the rulers and the nobles paid their debt there and made offerings.
statements.doctrinal_note: Note the doubly narrowed claim: the heading does not say that everyone born in this trecena slandered, but that this was told of those born in one named house of it, the ninth. Book 4 routinely locates an augury at a specific day inside a trecena, which is precisely the resolution a twenty-sign personality table cannot represent.

statements.nahuatl: qujtoqujlitica yn jpan vme ocelutl, ioan ei quauhtli, navi cozcaquauhtli, macujlli olin, chiquacen tecpatl: in jzqujtetl in tonalli mjtoaia amo qualli, amo ieccan,
statements.engine_rendering: There follow upon it Two Ocelot, and Three Eagle, Four Vulture, Five Movement, Six Flint. All of these days were said to be not good, not a favourable place.
statements.doctrinal_note: Kernel cross-check: trecena 5 runs acatl, ocelotl, cuauhtli, cozcacuauhtli, ollin, tecpatl, quiahuitl, xochitl, cipactli, ehecatl, calli, cuetzpalin, coatl. The witness lists only the first six positions here and agrees with the kernel on all of them; unlike the chapters with complete lists, this one breaks off, and the pack does not silently complete it.

statements.nahuatl: Auh injc mjtoa: amo ieccan, in aqujn ipan tlacatia pilli, anoco maceoalli, atle cenca imaceoal, ilhujl catca, can iuhqujn ehecatl ipa povia inemiliz, êcatocoia, atle itlaanca, inelhoaio mochioaia: ipampa in jtonalpan quetzalcoatl, êecatl otlacat, ca njman iuhcan oquiz, no iuhquj ipan muchioaia, intla cioatl,
statements.engine_rendering: And so it is said that it is not a favourable place: he who was born on it, noble or commoner, had no great deserving, no great portion; his life went as the wind goes, it was carried off by the wind, it had nothing to take hold of, it grew no root - because he was born on the day sign of Quetzalcoatl, of Wind, and so he simply came out that way. The same befell a woman.
statements.doctrinal_note: The augury is an argument by likeness to the patron deity, not an assertion about character: the life of one born on Quetzalcoatl's day is wind-borne because Quetzalcoatl is the wind. Stripping the deity out and keeping 'rootless, unstable' as a trait would keep the conclusion while discarding the reason the source gives for it.

statements.nahuatl: intla aca ipan otlacat izqujlhujtl oc conchololtiaia, qujchieltiaia in chiconqujavitl qujnjquac caltiaia inic qujtocamacazque, ipampa ic qujpatia in jtonal, vncan qujieccaquixtia, ieccan qujca, chicoqualtia, ic conjttilia, in aco ca itla ilhujl, imaceoal, muchioatiuh intla nemiz, intla uel oapaoaz, intla uel moquetzaz ipampa oc vncan in chicomatl qujtlaliaia, vel qujtemachiaia in chiconqujavitl.
statements.engine_rendering: If someone was born on any of these days they would let it pass by, they would make him wait for Seven Rain; only then did they bathe him, in order to give him his name - because by this they cured his day sign. There they brought him out well; he came out in a favourable place, he was made somewhat good, and so they contrived that he might come to have some portion, some deserving, if he lived, if he was well reared, if he stood up well. For that reason they set Seven Water there, and they trusted greatly in Seven Rain.
statements.doctrinal_note: Decisive against any 'your day sign is X' product. The tonalpouhque deliberately moved the child's naming off the birth day onto a better one, and the text says outright that this cured the day sign ('qujpatia in jtonal'). The operative sign was chosen, not merely observed - so a birth date alone never determined the reading even inside the tradition.

statements.nahuatl: [chiquacen]tetl machiotl, in jtoca ce mjqujztli: ioan in qualli tonalli itech ca, qujlmach itonal in Tezcatlipuca: auh mjec in ventli, in nextlaoalli injc qujmaviztiliaia, ioan cenca qujnpapaqujltiaia in tlatlacoti.

statements.nahuatl: Auh in aqujn ipa tlacatia itonal ce mjqujztli: mjtoaia mocujltonoz, motlamachtiz, intla pilli, anoco can maceoaltzintli, muchi inemactia, itech acia, itech pachivia, in mavicotl: iquac in tlauellamaceoa, mocnomati: auh intlacamo uellamaceoa, ca can yneujian conmocaujlia, qujmjtlacalhuja yn jtonal.
statements.engine_rendering: And of the one born on it, whose day sign was One Death, it was said: he will be rich, he will prosper - whether a noble or only a poor commoner, everything was granted him, honour reached him and settled upon him - at the time when he did penance well, when he was humble. And if he did not do penance well, then of his own accord he abandons it; he spoils his own day sign.
statements.doctrinal_note: The cleanest statement of the doctrine in the chapters surveyed here. The good outcome is explicitly time-bound to conduct ('iquac in tlauellamaceoa, mocnomati'), and the failure is reflexive: 'yneujian conmocaujlia, qujmjtlacalhuja yn jtonal' - by his own doing he lets it go, he damages his day sign. The person acts on the sign, not only the sign on the person.

statements.nahuatl: Injc matlactli oce capitulo: itechpa tlatoa, injc chicontetl machiotl, in jtoca ce qujavitl: ioan in amo qualli tonalli, in jtech catca: quilmach in aqujque vncan tlacatia, nanaoalti catca, ioan tetlachivianj, tlatlacatecolo: auh in tlacatecolotl, ca iehoatl qujtoznequj in Diablo, achi muchi in calli itech pouhquj, in amo qualli, in amo iectli: canjio inic matlactetl vmey qualli.

statements.engine_rendering: Eleventh chapter, which tells of the seventh sign, named One Rain, and of the bad day-fortune that was upon it. It is told that those born then were sorcerers, and workers of enchantment, and owl-men - and 'tlacatecolotl' means the Devil. Almost all the houses belonging to it were not good, not right; only the thirteenth was good.
statements.doctrinal_note: The gloss equating tlacatecolotl with 'el Diablo' is the friar's editorial hand inside the Nahuatl column, and it is quoted here as part of the witness rather than removed: this corpus is a colonial evangelising compilation as well as a Nahua one. The final clause is also a datum against uniform trecena readings - the compiler counts the houses one by one, and one of the thirteen escapes.

statements.nahuatl: Moquetza ce qujaujtl: injn mjtoaia, njman amo qualli tonalli, motqujtica teuhtli, tlacolli, icnoiotl, icnotlacaiotl, tlaciaujliztli, tlacococaviliztli, teopouhcaiotl, atle onqujcaliztli, atle oneoatinemjliztli:

statements.nahuatl: ipampa in jpan, y, tonalli, iuh mjtoa: ca vncan temoia, in moteneoa cioateteo, atlacacemelleque, teca mocaiaoanj: ic cenca qujntlaquauhnaoatiaia, in tepilhoan, in aiac qujcaz, aiac vtli qujtocaz: can cali onozque: iuh qujmjlhujaia maca xonqujcaca, anmotenamjctizque, ca temo, ca tlalpan aci in cioapipilti: ic qujntlamauhcaittiliaia in tetaoan: injc amo aca tennecujliviz, ixnecujliujz, tenpatziujz, itech qujneuaz:
statements.engine_rendering: ...because on this day sign, thus it is said, there descended those called the Cihuateteo, who are ill-omened and who mock people. For that reason they strictly commanded the children that none should go out, that none should take the road, that they should stay indoors. Thus they said to them: do not go out, you will meet them face to face, for they descend, the Cihuapipiltin reach the ground. By this the fathers made them afraid of them, so that no one's mouth should be twisted, no one's eye pulled awry, no one's lips withered, so that it should not fasten on him.
statements.doctrinal_note: The practical content of a bad day in Book 4 is a rule about what to do that day - keep the children in - not a claim about people born on it. The palsy symptoms listed (twisted mouth, pulled eye) are what the day is guarded against.

statements.nahuatl: Injc caxtolli capitulo: itechpa tlatoa, injc chicuetetl machiotl, in jtoca ce malinalli: ioan in amo qualli tonalli in jtech ca, auh qujl injc ontetl calli qualli: ioan in jxqujch oc cequj chicunauhtetl in jxqujch oc cequj, in jtech vmpeoa injc chicunauhtetl calli, ie injc matlactetl, ioan injc oce, injc omome, inic vmei, qujlmach qualli catca.

statements.engine_rendering: Fifteenth chapter, which tells of the eighth sign, named One Grass, and of the bad day-fortune that was upon it; and it is told the second house was good, and all the rest from the ninth house onward - that is, the tenth, and the eleventh, the twelfth, the thirteenth - it is told these were good.
statements.doctrinal_note: A 'bad' trecena in which five of the thirteen houses are counted good. The chapter heading itself enumerates them, which is why the pack encodes trecena membership separately from trecena valuation: the two are not the same claim.

statements.nahuatl: Moquetza ce malinalli, injn mjtoa: njman amo qualli tonalli, tequanj, imacaxonj, in aqujn ipa tlacatia, can motolinjtinenca, tel qujttaia in jneiollaliliz: auh can ompoli, can onqujztiqujca,
statements.engine_rendering: One Grass rises up: this is said to be in no way a good day sign - a wild beast, a thing to be feared. Whoever was born on it went about only in want; yet he did find his consolation, and then it perished, it passed straight away.
statements.doctrinal_note: 'tequanj' - a beast of prey - is Book 4's standard epithet for a dangerous day sign. Even here the source qualifies: 'tel qujttaia in jneiollaliliz', he did see his consolation. The concessive 'tel' recurs throughout the corpus and is the grammatical marker of its refusal to give unmixed verdicts.

statements.nahuatl: auh in aqujn ipan tlacatia, aiamo caltiaia, qujn jpan caltiaia, in ey ocelotl, cemilhujtonalli, iuh qujtoaia, in tonalpouhque, ca muchipa qualca in eitioaia, amo netenmachoia, iehoatl injc qujoallatotoqujliaia tonalpouhque, injc achi vncan qujqualtiliaia itonal, in jpan tlacatia ce malinalli.
statements.engine_rendering: And whoever was born on it, they did not yet bathe him; they bathed him only on Three Ocelot, a day sign of the day-count. Thus said the day-counters: the third is always a good place; nothing is feared there. For this reason the day-counters put it off to that day, so that they might thereby make somewhat better the day sign of the one born on One Grass.
statements.doctrinal_note: The second explicit mitigation in the pack, from a different chapter than the One Reed case on folio 21r: the same technique, deferring the bathing and naming to a better day, applied to a different bad sign. Two independent attestations make it a standing practice, not an isolated remark - and it means the tradition itself did not treat the birth day as the final word.

statements.nahuatl: Moquetza ce coatl: injn mjtoaia, qualli tonalli: in aqujn ipa tlacatia, qujtoaia: ilhujle, maceoale iez, mocujltonoz, oniez in qujquaz, in qujz, auh in iaoc, in iaopan, oqujchtiz, tiacauhtiz, momavizcotiz panvetziz, mavicoaz, moteniotiz, aco tlatocatiz, tecutiz,
statements.engine_rendering: One Serpent rises up: this was said to be a good day sign. Of the one born on it they said: he will have a portion, he will have deserving, he will be rich, he will have what to eat and what to drink; and in war, on the battlefield, he will prove a man, a brave warrior, he will win honour, he will rise high, he will be esteemed, he will gain a name, perhaps he will rule, will be a lord.
statements.doctrinal_note: The good-sign formula, stratified by station and by sex as in chapter 1; the clause for the woman follows immediately and runs on to folio 37v, where she is described as a gatherer and keeper who provides for her children.

statements.nahuatl: auh ioan mjtoa, macivi in iuhquj in inemac mochioa, in jpan tlacati (ca ie omjto mjieccan) intlacamo iê vellamaceoa, intlacamo vel monotza, catle vnqujca, ca ixcoian conmocaujlia, qujmjxcaoaltia, qujmopolhuja, qujmopopolhuja, in jmaceoal ocatca:
statements.engine_rendering: And it is also said: even though such is made the portion of the one born on it - as has already been said in many places - if he does not do penance well, if he does not take counsel with himself well, nothing comes of it; for of his own accord he lets it go, he deprives himself of it, he loses it, he destroys it utterly - what had been his deserving.
statements.doctrinal_note: Note the compiler's own aside, 'ca ie omjto mjieccan' (this has already been said in many places): Book 4 is aware that the forfeiture clause is its recurring structure and not an occasional remark. The following lines list the specific vices - taking work lightly, sloth, sleeping late, resenting instruction - by which the loss happens.

statements.nahuatl: Ioan mjtoa: in jpan in ce coatl, cenca qujqualittaia in puchteca, in oztomeca, in jaque, in nênemjnj, in vecacalaqujnj, intonalpan catca, intlapoalpan catca, iehoatl qujtztivia, vncan vmpeoaia in veca:

statements.doctrinal_note: A trecena can be read as an occasion rather than a nativity: One Serpent is here an electional day for departure, chosen by a profession. This is the same corpus supplying election, not character.

statements.nahuatl: Injc cempoalli oce capitulo: itechpa tlatoa, injc matlactetl machiotl, in jtoca ce tecpatl: ioan qujl qualli in jtonallo, auh qujl in aqujque vncan tlacatia chicaoaque catca, ioan tequjoacatia: auh qujl in cioa vncan tlacatia oqujchiolloque catca, muchi in veli catca, cenca uel qujnextiaia in jntlatquj: auh qujl itonal catca in Vitzilopuchtli, in jtech pouhquj catca, in jtequjuh catca iiaoiotl, qujl no itonal in Camaxtle: auh in jquac vmpeoaia injn machiotl, qujlhujqujxtiliaia, auh qujl muchi qualli catca in jzqujlhujtl, matlaqujlhujtl vmei.

statements.engine_rendering: Twenty-first chapter, which tells of the tenth sign, named One Flint, and it is told its day-fortune was good; and it is told that those born then were strong, and became bearers of office; and it is told that the women born then were manly of heart, capable of everything, and made their property greatly increase. statements.doctrinal_note: The same precaution as on One Rain (folio 27v), attached to a different sign. What the corpus supplies for these days is a rule of conduct for everyone alive that day; nothing here is a statement about people born under the sign.

statements.engine_rendering: Twenty-third chapter, which tells of the twelfth sign, named One Lizard. statements.nahuatl: Moquetza ce cuetzpalli: inin qujqualittaia, qujtoaia: in aquj̄ ipan tlacatia, cenca chicaoac, chicaoacanacaio aic cenca mococoa: auh intla cana oalhuetzi aquen conmati, meuhtiuetzi, popoxiuhteoa:

statements.nahuatl: Niman oalmoquetza in ce olin: injn qujtoaia, can chico qualli in aqujn vncan tlacati, in oqujchtli, in cioatl in vellamaceoa, in vel monotza, in uel mooapaoa, iehoatl qujcaia, qujttaia in jmaceoal, in jnemac:
statements.engine_rendering: Then One Movement rises up: of this they said it is good only by halves. Whoever was born then, man or woman, who did penance well, who took counsel with himself well, who was well brought up - that one came out, that one saw his deserving, his portion.
statements.doctrinal_note: 'can chico qualli' - good only on one side. The sign is stated to be half-good before any person is described, and the good half is then made to depend on three named practices: penance, self-counsel, upbringing. The other half follows in the next paragraph.

statements.nahuatl: auh intlacamo vel monotza, intlacamo uel mozcalti: can icuepca in qujmonamictiaia icnoiotl, itech eoatinemj, can nentlacatl, acan petzitl, can quauhtlamelaoa, aanemj, can iuh onioa, acan ixtona. Et
statements.engine_rendering: But if he did not take counsel with himself well, if he was not well reared, then in exchange what he met with was misery; it went about clinging to him; he was a mere waste of a man, nowhere polished, he blundered straight into the woods, he lived aimlessly, he simply went off, nowhere came into the light.

orthography_note: Quoted Nahuatl follows the pilot's convention: c-cedilla is written c, and the vowels a-circumflex, a-tilde, o-tilde and o-circumflex are written a, a, o and o. Every quotation is otherwise a verbatim slice of the pinned witness, taken mechanically rather than retyped. The unmodified reading is always recoverable from the hash-pinned witness named in each statement, which is the authority; the stripped form is a convenience, not the text.
